reasons_add: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports al-Zajjāj's nominative analysis, supplying an implicit nūdiya annahu.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports al-Zajjāj's nominative parse with an implicit nūdiya annahu.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the good increases and multiplies, and that blessing is associated specifically with good.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites Abū Ṭālib's verse applying blessing to a stranger's grave and ripe pomegranates and olives; he also gives barakaka Allāh as an example with a direct object and no preposition.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports al-Dānī transmitting wa-man ḥawlahā min al-malāʾika from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and ʿIkrima.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan identifying God, while rejecting some formulations of that identification. He also reports al-Thaʿlabī's Torah analogy: God's coming from Sinai, Seir and Paran signifies prophetic commands appearing in those regions; Paran is a mountain of Mecca.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya also reports Ibn ʿAbbās identifying man as the light.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits Ibn Jinnī's reading tabārakat al-nār wa-man ḥawlahā, which directly names the fire as blessed.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes the intended sense of the God-referent reports to be God's power and sovereignty manifested in the fire as Moses perceived it, rejecting some literal formulations.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports al-Ḥasan and Ibn ʿAbbās naming both angels and Moses.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows the glorification to be an aside addressed to Muḥammad.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this declaration rules out likeness or modality in the divine call on either account of its speaker.
Al-Sāmarrāʾī explains that Qaṣaṣ specifies the call's direction and location in 28:30, while Naml omits them because its account is concise.

question: 27:8/q12
position: Ibn Jinnī reports 'The fire and those around it were blessed' (tabārakat al-nār wa-man ḥawlahā).
reasons: Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits this distinct wording from Ibn Jinnī.
